claim: Biswajit Bhowmik, an advocate with the Bangladesh National Women Lawyers' Association (BNWLA), said at the 6 June 2026 Cox's Bazar roundtable that many people from Cox's Bazar go abroad by air holding a passport, visa and BMET card but are sent on 90-day visas, and after arriving get neither permission to stay nor any work and are forced to come home empty-handed.
target_section: A visit or tourist visa sold as a job
why_new: A lawyer handling returnees' cases describes workers who hold a BMET card yet travel on a 90-day visa; also belongs in "When the visa, the agency and the clearance are all real". He names no destination country.

claim: Naznin Akter, a Bangladeshi woman who returned from Malaysia, told a roundtable on technology-driven fraud and human trafficking held at the Prothom Alo office in Dhaka on 22 July 2026 that she was taken to Malaysia on a visit visa on 15 November 2025 for a promised restaurant job, and that she had been taught beforehand what to say at immigration.
target_section: A visit or tourist visa sold as a job
why_new: A dated Malaysia visit-visa case and a mechanism the section lacks: the traveller is coached on what to tell immigration.

claim: Sajal Baidya, 35, of Jagannathpur, Sunamganj, who had come home from Saudi Arabia about three years earlier, lost Tk 6 lakh a few months before March 2024 trying to go to Romania through a dalal and then engaged another dalal to go to Italy for Tk 13 lakh, a relative told Prothom Alo; he died under a train at Kulaura station, Moulvibazar, on 6 March 2024, and the railway police officer in charge said that, from talking to relatives, it appeared he had killed himself by jumping under the moving train.
target_section: Fake European work permits
why_new: A dated case of a Romania payment lost to a dalal followed by a second, larger payment to another dalal, ending in a death; no police action against the dalals is reported.

claim: The CID said in May 2024 that Jannat Trade International took BDT 5 lakh 12 thousand each from three people with a promise of well-paid jobs in Kyrgyzstan and gave them so-called Kyrgyzstan visas and air tickets; when they went to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on 7 April, immigration police found no record of their visas online and their journey was stopped.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: A dated Kyrgyzstan fake-visa case with the price and how it was caught (immigration's online visa check).

claim: In the Jannat Trade International case, a case was filed at Paltan police station, Dhaka, under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act, and the CID arrested three people, including the firm's proprietor, Ibrahim Mallik Nahid, whom it called the head of the ring (reported 7 May 2024).
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: Shows a fake-visa airport case registered as trafficking, not only as fraud.

claim: Lailul Haque (34) of Kafura village, Sherpur upazila, Bogura, told Prothom Alo in May 2024 that Abdul Alim, a businessman of the Sherua area who sends people abroad, sent him to Malaysia on a fake visa on 6 June 2023, and that he was sent back to Bangladesh after six days in jail.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: A dated Malaysia fake-visa case that ended in jail on arrival and return.

claim: A sub-inspector of Sherpur police station, Bogura, told Prothom Alo that Abdul Alim took Tk 5 lakh 70 thousand from Lailul Haque to send him to Malaysia as a worker, and Tk 2 lakh 30 thousand, Tk 3 lakh 14 thousand, Tk 2 lakh 70 thousand and Tk 3 lakh 50 thousand from four other young men; Lailul Haque put the total for the five at Tk 17 lakh 34 thousand.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: Amounts one local broker took from five men of two unions.

claim: Abdul Gani (30) of Shushuti village, Fulbaria, Mymensingh, said he gave Shafiqul Islam, known locally as a manpower broker, a total of BDT 6 lakh 10 thousand to go to Turkey; Shafiqul took his passport and money, kept him waiting a year and a half, then said Turkey was not possible and he would be sent to Saudi Arabia within 20 days, and on 18 February (2025) gave him an air ticket in the name of 'Jazeera Airways' and a visa, both of which turned out to be fake.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: A dated village-level case with the destination switched and both ticket and visa forged.

claim: RAB said in May 2025 that Shafiqul Islam (42) of Patira village, Fulbaria, Mymensingh, cheated people by making fake tickets in the names of 'Jazeera Airways', 'Air Arabia', 'Salam Air', 'Egypt Air' and others.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: Fake airline tickets in named airlines' names as part of the package.

claim: RAB-14 detained Shafiqul Islam at Technopara, Joydebpur, Gazipur, on the night of 29 May 2025 and handed him to Fulbaria police station; RAB-14's commander, Naymul Hasan, said he had been cheating village people for about three years and a case would be filed under the regular law, and the Fulbaria officer-in-charge said the complaint would be verified and legal action taken.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: What the authorities did, and that no case had yet been registered when reported.

claim: Local residents alleged that Shafiqul Islam took nearly BDT 1 crore in a few years on promises of sending people abroad for work, and the two complainants said many people in nearby areas had been cheated through him.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: Scale of one village broker, as alleged.

claim: On 23 September 2025 the CID arrested Josna Khatun (35), of Daljitpur village, Narail, in Ibrahimpur, Kafrul, Dhaka; the CID said she is the named main accused in a fraud case at Paltan police station and that the ring first lured people with jobs abroad, then took large sums through several bank accounts and gave them fake visas.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: A dated Italy fake-visa ring with payment through bank accounts, not only cash or mobile money.

claim: According to the September 2025 report, the Josna Khatun ring promised high-paid jobs in Italy and handed over forged visas, and also took money on promises of placing people in important government posts; its network covers Faridpur, Narail, Narsingdi, Kishoreganj, Chandpur, Chattogram and other districts.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: Destination (Italy), the districts covered, and that the same ring also sold government jobs.

claim: According to the September 2025 report, an earlier-arrested active member of the same ring, Milon Mia of Faridpur, was found in the investigation to have collected people from different areas in the name of sending them abroad, and the ring took several crore taka from more than a hundred people.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: The division of roles (a district-level collector feeding a Dhaka ring) and the scale. Note: the article's opening line says 'hundreds of crores' while the CID detail says several crore from over a hundred people.

claim: Sujan Mia of Chhatak upazila, who said he was caught in France and returned to Bangladesh, said on 18 April 2026 that when he later tried for an Australian visa a broker and an agency took BDT 17 lakh from him and gave him a fake visa.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: A deportee cheated again at home: BDT 17 lakh for a fake Australian visa.

claim: Tanzim Ul Haque, a senior officer at the Sandwip branch of Probashi Kallyan Bank, told Prothom Alo in May 2026 that in many cases they see fraudulent contracts between a fake employer and the worker, and that many people still sell their homestead to go abroad and end up in trouble.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: A bank loan officer's first-hand statement that fake employer-worker contracts reach PKB.

claim: People concerned told Prothom Alo in November 2026 that until then a demand letter for up to seven workers needed no permission from the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry, that there are allegations this was used to bring in fake appointment letters in the name of sending workers, and that after the 4 November 2026 instruction every demand letter must be approved first.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: The loophole behind small-batch fake demand letters (seven workers or fewer needed no Ministry permission) and its closure.

claim: The UAE Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE) named five signs of a fake job offer, Gulf News reported (Prothom Alo, 22 November 2026): being asked to open a new bank account in your own name as part of recruitment; being asked for confidential bank account details by an unverified person or company; a demand for money to confirm the job or complete recruitment; being asked to receive money into your account or transfer it on to another account; and insistence on contact only through WhatsApp or another messaging app with no institutional phone number or address.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: Five official red flags from the UAE ministry; the section's UAE content covers only the offer check.

claim: MOHRE says every valid job offer issued through its system carries a specific serial number and a barcode, and a job seeker can verify an offer on the ministry's official website, in the 'MOHRE UAE' mobile app or by calling 600590000 (Prothom Alo, 22 November 2026, citing the ministry).
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: Adds what a real UAE offer looks like (serial number, barcode) and two more ways to check (app, phone 600590000) beyond inquiry.mohre.gov.ae.

claim: MOHRE said that anyone meeting these conditions after a job offer should stop the process at once and verify, and should give no money or personal information until the offer letter is confirmed genuine.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: The ministry's instruction on what to do when a flag appears.

claim: MOHRE's labour market observatory said more than 26 lakh people contacted the ministry through its channels for services and verification in the third quarter of 2026 (July to September); according to BMET, more than 70 per cent of workers who leave Bangladesh each year go to Middle Eastern countries.
target_section: Fake visa, demand letter or job offer
why_new: Scale of use of the UAE verification channels; low priority.

claim: On Tuesday 6 October 2026, UK Home Office immigration officers raided several London addresses and arrested two people on suspicion of fraud and immigration offences, accused of making fake documents, including staged photos and forged papers, that presented asylum seekers as gay, for up to £4,500 each; phones, jewellery and thousands of pounds were seized and a third person was arrested on suspicion of staying illegally.
target_section: NEW: Asylum claims built on a false story
why_new: The guide has no case of a bought asylum story.

claim: The ring is believed to have helped prepare dozens of asylum claims by Bangladeshi men saying they were gay and that their lives would be in danger if returned, and the Home Office said many Bangladeshi men first claimed asylum on political grounds and, after refusal, claimed again as gay.
target_section: NEW: Asylum claims built on a false story
why_new: The mechanism: a second, invented claim after a refused political claim.

claim: Chris Foster, regional head of the Home Office's criminal investigations, said intelligence showed the suspects charged each asylum seeker at least £1,000 and at most £4,500 for fake papers, which could include support letters from 'Apnajon', a Bangladeshi LGBT organisation based in Whitechapel, east London, staged photos meant to show the applicant as gay, and letters from someone claiming to be in a same-sex relationship with the applicant.
target_section: NEW: Asylum claims built on a false story
why_new: The price and what the package contains.

claim: According to Chris Foster, the October 2026 arrests centred on fake asylum claims linked to 'Apnajon', and the organisation came under suspicion after caseworkers saw the same kind of information repeated across several suspicious claims, followed by months of investigation.
target_section: NEW: Asylum claims built on a false story
why_new: How such claims are detected: identical stories across files.

claim: The UK Home Office was reviewing more than a hundred asylum claims linked to the ring in October 2026, and Chris Foster said some fake claims had undoubtedly already been approved.
target_section: NEW: Asylum claims built on a false story
why_new: Even approved claims are being reopened.

claim: A BBC investigation published in April 2026 reported that lawyers and advisers were helping some migrants claim asylum as gay, and secretly recorded a legal adviser, Tanisa Khan, saying she could arrange a 'full package' including photos taken at gay clubs and other evidence.
target_section: NEW: Asylum claims built on a false story
why_new: Who sells the package (legal advisers).

claim: UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said that those who profited from asylum fraud would be prosecuted, their illegal earnings seized and all their operations in the country shut, and that fraudulent asylum claims would be cancelled and the claimants removed from the country; the UK government says conviction for asylum fraud can carry up to 10 years in prison.
target_section: NEW: Asylum claims built on a false story
why_new: Consequence for the applicant, not only the seller.

claim: Kawsar Khan, an immigration lawyer in Sydney, wrote in Prothom Alo on 26 November 2024 that the main condition of Australia's work visas is that an Australian business sponsors the applicant, that only an 'approved sponsor' approved by Australia's immigration department can nominate someone, that getting a job through such a sponsor from Bangladesh is in practice very hard, and that there are precedents of lakhs of taka being taken in the name of a sponsor.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The real rule the scam imitates: only an approved sponsor can nominate.

claim: Kawsar Khan wrote in November 2024 that proof of English skill is a mandatory condition for an Australian work visa, and that immigration experts say anyone who claims the visa can be had without proof of English should be identified as a fraud ring.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: A concrete red flag from a named immigration lawyer.

claim: Kawsar Khan wrote in November 2024 that Australian immigration law changes almost every year, and that fraud rings use wrong explanations of such changes and flashy news to cause financial loss to many people who want to go abroad.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Mechanism: scams ride on news of real rule changes (see also the 2026 farm-visa rumour).

claim: According to Kawsar Khan in November 2024, an applicant for Australia's subclass 482 work visa at that time needed at least two years' experience in the same occupation within the previous five years (for example, a Bangladeshi applying as a restaurant manager), and the immigration department had proposed cutting this to one year.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The experience requirement a real 482 applicant had to meet in 2024; a proposal, so the current rule needs an official source.

claim: A Prothom Alo explainer of 6 August 2026 set out the real Canadian work permit process: a genuine job offer from a Canadian organisation; the employer applies to the Canadian government for an LMIA (Labour Market Impact Assessment, proof that no citizen or permanent resident was found for the post) and gets it approved; the applicant submits the job offer, passport, proof of education and professional qualification, proof of language skill and, as required, a health examination; after biometrics, security checks and assessment the immigration authority decides; and the work permit itself is issued on arrival on the border officer's final approval.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The real five-step process against which a Canada offer can be compared; the guide has none.

claim: The August 2026 explainer said not every Canadian job needs an LMIA: work permits are also given without one under international agreements, special programmes and for certain occupations.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Qualifies the LMIA rule so the guide does not overstate it.

claim: According to the August 2026 explainer, Canada has nothing like Saudi Arabia's kafil (sponsor) system in which a sponsor can arrange a visa: only the federal government issues Canadian visas, and even provincial governments have no power to issue one.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Corrects the Gulf-shaped belief that a visa can be bought from a sponsor.

claim: The August 2026 explainer listed what Canada fraudsters claim: '100 per cent guaranteed visa' (১০০ শতাংশ গ্যারান্টি ভিসা), 'a job without an interview' (ইন্টারভিউ ছাড়াই চাকরি), 'Canadian permanent residence (PR) in two or three months', 'a high-paid job with no qualifications', 'a special government quota' (সরকারি বিশেষ কোটা) and 'no language skill needed'.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The sales phrases used for Canada, in Bangla.

claim: The August 2026 explainer said the Canadian government or immigration department gives no one an advance assurance of a visa, every application is checked separately, and no person, agency or representative can guarantee visa approval.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: A guarantee is itself the red flag.

claim: Analysing recent incidents and various past frauds, the August 2026 explainer said Canada fraudsters typically make fake job offer letters using well-known organisations' logos, show copies of forged LMIAs or work permits, send fake visa approval letters, build copies of government websites, use the photos or identities of people living in Canada on social media, and press for a quick decision and an advance payment.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The full kit of trust-building devices for Canada offers.

claim: The August 2026 explainer said to check four things on a Canada job offer: that the employer really exists, by matching its address, phone number and website; that the pay, workplace, duties and contract terms in the offer letter are realistic; that the email came from the organisation's own domain and not a free email service; and, if told to verify the visa on a website, that it really is a government website.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Four concrete checks for a Canada offer.

claim: Experts cited in the August 2026 explainer advised against sending large sums to a personal bank account or mobile banking number, said receipts for every payment should be kept and any document read and understood before signing, and said that in case of doubt a Canada-authorised immigration consultant or lawyer can be consulted.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Payment advice and who can give a second opinion.

claim: The August 2026 explainer said a Canadian work permit is a temporary permission and never a right to live there permanently, so advertising that 'a work permit means guaranteed PR' is misleading; permanent residence can be applied for later only on meeting qualification, work experience, language and programme conditions.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Counters the 'work permit = PR' pitch.

claim: The August 2026 explainer said about 6 per cent of Canada's population was unemployed and lakhs of international students already in Canada were looking for jobs, and that without a good score in IELTS (English) or in TEF or TCF (the French tests) a Canadian job visa 'is not for you'.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Why a no-qualification Canada job offer is implausible: competition and the language-test bar.

claim: Kawsar Khan reported on 11 August 2026 that law enforcers had recently arrested several rings in Dhaka and elsewhere accused of building copies of Australian government websites and giving fake sponsorships and 'work visit visas'.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Shows the pattern is repeated across several rings, not one case.

claim: The Australian High Commission in Dhaka said in a recent warning, reported on 11 August 2026, that to avoid fake migration agents people should go to a registered migration agent or a lawyer for any visa advice.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: An official warning from the destination's mission.

claim: Under Australian law an agent giving visa advice or services must be registered with OMARA (the Office of the Migration Agents Registration Authority), and any registered agent's name or number can be checked free on the online list at www.mara.gov.au, Kawsar Khan wrote in August 2026.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: A check that exists, with where and the cost (free).

claim: According to Kawsar Khan in August 2026, a registered Australian migration agent must charge only a fair and reasonable fee, give the client a written agreement or written information on the cost and scope of the service before starting, and tell the applicant the result of the application as soon as it is received.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: What a genuine agent is bound to do, so its absence can be spotted.

claim: Kawsar Khan wrote in August 2026 that there is no way to get an Australian work visa directly without a language test or skills assessment, that the Department of Home Affairs alone has authority to grant a visa and no person, employer, organisation or lawyer can guarantee one, and that an Australian employer can apply to sponsor a worker from abroad only when suitable skilled people are not available locally, which is costly and slow.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The real rule behind Australian work visas, and that visas are not bought and sold as in the Gulf.

claim: Kawsar Khan listed in August 2026 the promises that mark an Australia fraud: 'recruitment for over a hundred posts with no experience', 'guaranteed permanent citizenship in two months from a work visa' and 'no interview or English skill needed'.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The sales phrases used for Australia.

claim: According to Kawsar Khan in August 2026, Australia fraudsters make wholly forged job appointment letters on the letterhead and logo of a well-known Australian organisation and then demand an advance, and use overseas or internet phone numbers to make it seem the call came from Australia.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Forged offer letters and spoofed numbers for Australia.

claim: Kawsar Khan's August 2026 checklist: check the agent's registration number before paying anything for a visa; send no large sum to a personal bank or mobile banking number and collect a written receipt for every payment; follow only the government's official immigration website, immi.homeaffairs.gov.au; and on a job offer from an employer, go to that organisation's own website, take the contact details from there and verify the offer.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Four concrete checks with the official site named.

claim: Tanvir Ahmed, one of the Bangladeshis living in Australia quoted in an August 2026 Prothom Alo article, said many in Bangladesh think a visa comes for lakhs of taka but a work visa is impossible there without proof of skill and language, and Sharmin Sultana said fraudsters now send fake links that look exactly like government websites.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Expatriates' own account of what they see; low priority.

claim: Harun ur Rashid, a businessman in Leppington, Sydney, said a ring made a contract of about BDT 16 lakh with a relative of his to bring him on an agricultural visa with the lure of permanent citizenship in three years, though the relative lacked even the minimum English or occupational qualification for an ordinary work visa; the forgery became clear when the application number and the grant number were matched.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: A price (about BDT 16 lakh) for an Australia 'agricultural visa', and how it was caught.

claim: Kawsar Khan wrote in August 2026 that OMARA has taken disciplinary action against more than 61 registered migration advisers since 2021-22, and that in Australia itself several advisers' licences have been cancelled over allegations of lending their licences to unregistered fake brokers.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Even a registered adviser's number can be lent to an unregistered broker; action taken in Australia.

claim: Kawsar Khan advised in August 2026 that all Australian immigration business is done on the government's one official portal (homeaffairs.gov.au), that the truth of an offer can be checked by speaking on a government number or through the embassy, that no money should be sent to a personal bank or mobile account, and that the health examination should be done nowhere except at the clinic designated by the Australian High Commission in Dhaka.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Adds the medical rule: only the High Commission's designated clinic (compare the fake medical tests in 'Proof that is not proof').

claim: Kawsar Khan wrote in August 2026 that people who are told a document is forged often reply 'I have spent so much already, let me pay a bit more and see what happens', and call again only when stuck at the airport or abroad after losing their savings and homestead.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Why victims keep paying after a warning, from a practitioner of 17 years.

claim: Kawsar Khan, a registered Australian migration consultant, wrote on 2 October 2026 that there is no direct agricultural visa to Australia for Bangladeshis and that the brokers' trade in one is a fraud from start to finish; social media posts were claiming Australia was giving fast visas to Bangladeshi farm workers and that a visa would come in 10 to 15 days with no experience or English certificate.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: A current (autumn 2026) scam and a flat statement that the visa does not exist for Bangladeshis.

claim: Kawsar Khan traced the rumour to real news: from July 2026 Australia slowed processing of Working Holiday Maker visas, and on 17 September minister Tony Burke announced that agriculture and fisheries would be added to the priority list for skilled visa processing and that first-year Working Holiday applications would again be processed at normal speed; what Australian media called 'faster visas for farms' became 'agricultural visas for Bangladeshis' in Bangladesh, though the announcement covered only people already eligible and citizens of specified countries.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Shows how a real announcement was twisted into the sales pitch.

claim: The main route for foreign farm workers into Australia is the Pacific Australia Labour Mobility scheme (PALM), which is open only to nine Pacific island countries (Fiji, Kiribati, Nauru, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu) and Timor-Leste; workers are selected through those countries' government labour-sending offices, and stay up to 9 months for seasonal work or one to four years on long-term contracts, Kawsar Khan wrote in October 2026.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The real farm-work scheme and why a Bangladeshi cannot be in it.

claim: Kawsar Khan wrote that the PALM scheme's official website itself says no one has to pay money or give a gift to join and the employer pays the airfare at the start, while people in Dhaka, Chattogram or Khulna were asking lakhs of taka in the name of an 'agricultural visa'.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The real scheme is free to the worker; any fee is the flag.

claim: According to Kawsar Khan in October 2026, brokers most often use the name of the Working Holiday visa and say anyone aged eighteen to thirty can apply; the visa goes only to citizens of specified countries, it has two types, subclass 417 and 462, and Bangladesh is in neither; India entered the list in 2024 under a trade agreement, and by lottery.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The half-truth brokers use (the age rule) and the fact that undoes it (Bangladesh is not on either list).

claim: Kawsar Khan wrote that the legal routes to Australia for Bangladeshis are the study visa, skilled migration visas and employer-nominated work visas, the employer-sponsored temporary one being the Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482) in force since December 2024; these need an occupation on the approved list, proof of skill, work experience, English, and an employer eligible to sponsor, and there is no easy, direct way to bring people from Bangladesh for ordinary work such as fruit picking or clearing fields.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The legitimate routes, stated once, against which offers can be compared.

claim: When an Australian visa is granted the approval letter carries a number that can be matched on the Australian government's checking service VEVO, Kawsar Khan wrote in October 2026, adding that new tricks keep appearing and in some cases more checking is needed even when the visa shows on VEVO.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: The official check (VEVO) and its limit, which ties to the 'visa shows online' trick.

claim: Kawsar Khan wrote that the conversation should end if someone cannot show a registered migration professional's number, cannot state the visa subclass and details, or talks of a 'visa in ten days'.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Three questions to put to anyone selling an Australian visa.

claim: In the same 17 September 2026 speech, according to Kawsar Khan, the minister said second-year Working Holiday visas would now go by lottery with 45,000 places against about 57,000 who qualified the year before, and third-year places would be only 5,000 against about 31,000; the National Farmers' Federation says these visa holders do one in seven farm jobs.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
why_new: Shows Australia is tightening, not opening; low priority, needs an official source.

claim: Kawsar Khan wrote in October 2026 that BMET (the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training) and the Bangladesh High Commission in Canberra should issue regular, plainly worded warnings about the 'agricultural visa' fraud.
target_section: NEW: Fake Australia and Canada work visas
placement: other: what authorities have not done
why_new: A gap: no Bangladeshi official warning is reported.

claim: The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare's February 2025 notice said that, to avoid being cheated by fake overseas job adverts circulated on social media such as Facebook and YouTube, the recruiting agency's or employer's information can be verified from BMET's website or the Probashbandhu call centre.
target_section: Online job adverts, Facebook and WhatsApp scams, and fake government sites
why_new: Names the two official channels the Ministry itself points to for checking an online job advert; the section's check points only to the fake-visa section.

claim: Afaz Uddin Molla (58), a Bangladeshi worker in Kuwait for 30 years, told Prothom Alo in June 2025 that in August 2024 he saw a social media advert saying 'a chance to go to Canada for little money' and rang the mobile number in the Facebook advert; the man who answered called himself Asadul Islam, said he was in Canada, could take him from Kuwait to Canada quickly, and that the salary there would be BDT 4 to 5 lakh.
target_section: Online job adverts, Facebook and WhatsApp scams, and fake government sites
why_new: A Canada Facebook-advert case aimed at a worker already in the Gulf.

claim: According to the case statement, the man calling himself Asadul took BDT 24 lakh from Afaz Uddin between August and December 2024 as the cost of a Canada visa, sent to several bKash numbers he supplied; Afaz Uddin was told again and again that the visa would come very soon, and then the phone number was switched off.
target_section: Online job adverts, Facebook and WhatsApp scams, and fake government sites
why_new: Amount, period, payment channel (several bKash numbers) and how contact ended.

claim: Roksana Akter, the complainant and wife of the Kuwait-based victim in the 2024 Canada case, told Prothom Alo that she asked many times to speak to 'Asadul' on a video call and he never agreed.
target_section: Online job adverts, Facebook and WhatsApp scams, and fake government sites
why_new: A red flag the article itself shows: the recruiter refuses video calls.

claim: Roksana Akter filed a case at Jatrabari police station, Dhaka, on 22 May 2025 naming a man called Asadul as the main accused with 20 to 25 unnamed associates, and police sources said the court ordered the CID to investigate.
target_section: Online job adverts, Facebook and WhatsApp scams, and fake government sites
why_new: What was done: a case in Dhaka by the family while the victim is abroad, sent to CID.
